extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts (monographs, proceedings, journals) for the American Mathematical Society
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and checklists for preparing and submitting mathematics monographs, proceedings articles, journal articles, and camera-ready materials to the American Mathematical Society, with detailed technical and formatting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS author package/template
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the template supplied in the author package for the particular AMS publication and the appropriate document style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author packages contain publication-specific instructions and style files; using them speeds publication, reduces errors, and ensures the published version matches the submission. Links to packages provided on AMS web pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redefine existing TEX/LaTeX/AMS commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not redeﬁne any existing LATEX, AMS-LATEX, or AMS-TEX commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redefinitions must be manually replaced by AMS staff, causing delays and errors. Include only macros actually used; define macros with \newcommand rather than \def where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only public CTAN packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only 'public' packages available from CTAN (the Comprehensive TEX Archive Network).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other macro packages may not be supported for conversion/processing; embed any other required macros in the preamble (only those actually used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid author-defined macros in topmatter and references
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic manuscripts, do not use author-deﬁned macros in author names, chapter titles, section headings, abstracts, or references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such macros may break indexing or online processing; keep topmatter and bibliographic items in plain, stable coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify page sizes or dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions; page sizes must conform to the specifications for the target series or journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS stylefiles set paging standards; altering them will conflict with production and may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid math in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the use of TEX math coding (especially dollar signs) in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles are supplied to online bibliographic services for indexing; math coding can produce inaccurate bibliographic listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title presence and descriptiveness (first page)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page must contain a descriptive title that is short but informative; for articles the first page must contain a descriptive title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague phrases such as 'some remarks about' or 'concerning'. Supply a shortened form of the title if needed for running heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title capitalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Monograph/chapter title capitalization: first and last words and all nouns, pronouns, adjectives, adverbs, verbs capitalized; articles, conjunctions, prepositions lowercased except first/last words. Article titles: only first word and proper nouns capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified capitalization conventions per publication type; AMS style files will apply uppercasing where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running heads content and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Running heads rules vary by publication: monographs—left (even) head chapter title uppercase, right (odd) head section title uppercase; proceedings—left head author name(s) uppercase; journals—left head author name(s) uppercase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorten titles/names as necessary to fit one line leaving room for page number; uppercasing may be applied automatically by AMS style files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter pagination for monographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily every chapter must begin on a new right-hand (odd-numbered) page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow book pagination conventions unless the author package for the series specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine and provide Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification numbers representing the primary and secondary subjects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide MSC numbers on the material for the copyright page; a list is available at www.ams.org/msc/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide grant/contract and copyright-page information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide grant/contract information (including grant number) and other details required for the copyright page; for translations include original publisher, copyright year, translator info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This material will be used to prepare the copyright page at AMS; include it in submissions as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for third-party material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for obtaining written permission to use another person's work (text, graphics, photos, tables, art), whether or not previously published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissions must be free of restrictions limiting AMS's ability to produce, publish, promote, and distribute the work in print or electronic form. Begin requesting permissions as soon as manuscript is accepted and send copies of permission letters with submission. AMS can assist if requested at least eight weeks before final submission due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-domain crediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission is not necessary for public-domain works (e.g., U.S. government publications or expired copyright), but credit should still be given to the originator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite originator even for public-domain items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: preferred formats and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic figures should be created at 100% size and saved in EPS format; if EPS unsupported, save in standard formats (TIFF, PICT, GIF, JPEG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fonts should be embedded or saved as outlines. Do not send application-dependent formats. Provide a paper copy of graphics for confirmation. For DVI submissions, EPS is required for embedded graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: captions and file contents
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic graphics submitted as part of an electronic manuscript, do not include the caption or page number in the graphics file; captions should be typeset from the source file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the electronic graphic version exactly matches the hard-copy version submitted; mismatches will delay publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: create at 100% and respect print area
rubrics_metrics.description: Create graphics at 100% of the printed size and do not exceed the dimensions of the print area for the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scaling is necessary, remember line weights scale too; thin lines may disappear if scaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: minimum line-weight and hairline prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The thinnest line weight that will reproduce clearly at high resolution is 0.5pt at 100%; do not specify 'hairline' weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rule lines are gray/colored, weight should be no thinner than 1pt. Graded line weights should increase by at least 0.5pt increments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: screened fills limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Screened fills should be no less than 15% (less prints as white) and no greater than 85% (greater prints as black).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid screening values outside these bounds to ensure legibility in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: text in graphics as outlines and bitmap DPI guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Text in graphics should be font outlines rather than bitmaps; bitmapped characters in line art should be at 1200 dpi; bitmaps of characters at 300 dpi or less may appear poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding font outlines is preferred because AMS uses a high-resolution imagesetter; if bitmaps used, ensure very high resolution for characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics resolution and preference
rubrics_metrics.description: For color images, resolution should be at least 300 pixels per inch for photographic images and 600 pixels per inch for line art when printed at 100%; preferred formats are EPS, TIFF, JPEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS normally does not include color in proceedings or print journals except by agreement; color images that print black-and-white will appear in color online as submitted. Preferred original submissions for color: glossy color photo, transparency/interneg, or color slide (in that order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics for nonelectronic originals
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonelectronic graphics should be drawn in black ink with clean unbroken lines on nonabsorbent paper; fonts used in graphics should match text fonts when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send originals of photographs or electronic artwork; avoid staples/clips that damage photos; use cardboard backing in mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded graphics inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If embedding calls to EPS files within TeX, do not include any path names for included EPS files; give only the filename (e.g., \includegraphics{fig1.eps}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using boxedeps.tex, include \SetRokickiEPSFSpecial immediately after inputting boxedeps.tex when creating DVI/PostScript to send to AMS. Include printed copies of all graphics with printed output of the TeX file. Submit separate file for each graphic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed macro packages for embedding graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use graphicx package for LaTeX; for AMS-TEX use epsf.tex or boxedeps.tex when calling external EPS files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS does not provide these macro files; they are available on CTAN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics placement and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures/tables should be numbered consistently, have an in-text reference, be placed on the page where referenced or as close as possible, and appear within the same section as their first text reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally place figures/tables at top or bottom of a page; a figure/table may appear unnumbered in-place when integral to text. Do not allow graphics to extend into margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placeholder spacing for graphics in nonelectronic camera-ready submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When leaving blank space for graphics to be inserted later, leave exact space for the graphic and specified spacing: at least 1.5 picas (1/4 inch, 0.7 cm) between text and top of graphic (if graphic follows text); 1 pica (1/6 inch, 0.4 cm) between the top of the graphic and the top of its caption; at least 1.5 picas (1/4 inch, 0.7 cm) from caption to text below (if text follows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these spacing rules so inserted graphics do not crowd surrounding text and so pagination remains acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations: display breaks, alignment, and width
rubrics_metrics.description: Check displayed equations carefully for proper breaking and alignment (per Swanson guidance) and ensure they do not exceed the page width for the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-line displays use structures defined in the amsmath user's guide or other recommended packages; avoid unacceptable math breaks between pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes: prepare using MakeIndex and include terms in TeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideally prepare indexes by including index terms directly in the TeX file to ensure correct page references; output from MakeIndex is processable only by LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using AMS-TEX contact AMS Technical Support for assistance. See AMS Author FAQ for common index questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission formats and copies (monographs/proceedings/journals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monographs: send two proof copies or a PDF to the appropriate book series editor and state intention to submit electronically (do not send source with initial proof). Proceedings: send two proof copies to the appropriate volume editor. Journals: follow initial submission instructions on the web (electronic submissions preferred); for nonelectronic send one copy to centralized manuscript processing and clearly indicate intended journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic source files are submitted after acceptance per Appendix A; do not send source files with initial proof copies unless instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of submission types
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic manuscript: a TeX file prepared using AMS-LATEX (strongly preferred) or AMS-TEX with appropriate style file. Nonelectronic manuscript: manuscript without usable electronic files, to be keyed by AMS. Camera-ready electronic submission: DVI/PostScript/PDF produced by author (graphics as EPS if DVI). Camera-ready nonelectronic: material scanned by AMS from author-submitted copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals generally do not accept camera-ready submissions; check publication-specific policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For camera-ready submissions, authors are responsible for final formatting and proofreading; AMS will print directly from what authors submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should read camera-ready instructions carefully and may send sample pages for checking prior to finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for paging (avoid widows/orphans and poor headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid widows (short line at top of page ending a paragraph), avoid centered heading at bottom with <2 lines following or at top with only 1 line preceding; ensure acceptable looking last page for proceedings (avoid single reference/affiliation/translated-by line alone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Swanson's guidelines for line breaks and permissible page breaks; AMS style files include penalties to prevent widows/orphans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A footnote must appear on the same page as its text reference. If a footnote must be split, break it between pages at a line that ends in the middle of a sentence so continuation to next page is evident; the footnote must at least begin on the same page as its reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure footnotes don't float away from their references; adjust paging as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required coding for online processing and linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles published online require uniform encoding using LaTeX conventions. Files must be self-contained (all macros except publicly distributed ones incorporated), use \cite for citations, and use \label with \ref or \eqref for cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only numbers, letters, and colons inside \label/\ref commands; other characters (including spaces) may fail to link properly and require AMS staff intervention. Non-AMS-LaTeX submissions are converted to AMS-LaTeX; plain TeX or basic LaTeX may require manual conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography/BibTeX handling
rubrics_metrics.description: All bibliographic data must be incorporated into the article file. If using BibTeX, insert the contents of the .bbl file into the .tex file; do not send the .bib file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the final .tex includes the complete bibliography for conversion and online processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement and suggested lengths (journals/proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS journal articles (except Book Reviews) must contain an abstract. Abstracts may be multiple paragraphs and include displayed material. Suggested upper limits are about 150 words for short papers and about 300 words for long papers; proceedings abstracts optional but suggested limits similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid bibliographic references in abstracts unless the bibliographic item is fully supplied (e.g., full citation instead of [3]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliation, addresses, and topmatter formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic or other affiliations should appear at the end of the article after the bibliography; current address (if different) should follow on a separate line; include email address if available. Unmarked footnotes on the first page should include primary MSC numbers (required), grant info (optional), and key words/phrases (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using AMS author packages, topmatter formatting is automatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro definition and processing preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals restrict macros: only public packages from CTAN allowed; other macros must be embedded and only macros actually used included; macros should be defined with \newcommand not \def.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals do not accept camera-ready submissions; hyperref will be added by Providence staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading responsibility for camera-ready submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must proofread their work before submitting; camera-ready submissions will not be proofread at the AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread carefully and follow camera-ready preparation instructions to avoid production errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement is sent to the author(s) when the accepted paper is received at the AMS; authors may transfer copyright or retain rights; signed form should be returned to Production Department immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If copyright transferred, authors may dedicate their paper to the public domain after 28 years; check forms and return promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready nonelectronic page layout dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Camera-ready nonelectronic submissions must follow type block dimensions: type block measure 30 by 50.5 picas (~5 x 8 3/8 inches) and chapter opening pages for monographs 30 by 43.5 picas (~5 x 7 1/4 inches). For proceedings first page length should be 39 picas (~6 1/2 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A printable template showing basic book page layout is available from AMS Book Author Resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and Appendix A procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A details options for submitting accepted work (web server preferred), email/FTP/physical media procedures, and checklists for electronic vs camera-ready submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Appendix A step-by-step instructions for packaging and sending files; sample FTP and email sessions provided for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and handling of processed-at-AMS submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions processed at AMS will be proofread by AMS editorial staff and authors usually receive page proofs; electronic manuscripts are preferred (AMS-LATEX/AMS-TEX). Nonelectronic manuscripts are keyed by AMS and should be double-spaced with generous margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number pages consecutively for nonelectronic manuscripts; double spacing helps with subscripts/superscripts and copyediting.
